title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook — Process, Runbooks, Postmortems, Rotations, Game Days, and Comms Templates
author: Maya Thompson
content:
Summary:
This playbook describes Redwood Inference's on-call and incident response processes. It consolidates incident lifecycle procedures, runbook templates, postmortem requirements, rotation and handoff rules, game day planning, and customer/status-page communication templates. Use this document as the single reference for responding to and learning from incidents that affect availability, correctness, or security of our inference platform.

1) Scope and intent
- Applies to all production services: inference-api, model-router, kv-cache, control-plane, billing-proxy, telemetry-ingest.
- Covers detection, escalation, mitigation, communication, post-incident review, and preventative actions.
- Intended audience: on-call engineers, SRE, incident commanders (IC), support, and product stakeholders.

2) Severity classification (use when triaging)
- P0 (Sev 0): Customer-impacting outage affecting >10% of requests or complete control-plane outage. Target time-to-ack: 5 minutes; IC: immediate.
- P1 (Sev 1): Large degradation (e.g., p95 latency > 5x SLO, error-rate > 5%) or major feature broken for many customers. Acknowledge within 15 minutes.
- P2 (Sev 2): Localized issues with limited impact, degraded metrics but workarounds exist. Acknowledge within 2 hours.
- P3 (Sev 3): Informational / scheduled maintenance / non-urgent bugs.

SLOs and alert thresholds (examples)
- inference-api: availability 99.95% monthly; alert if 5-min error-rate > 2% or p95 latency > 500ms.
- model-router: availability 99.9%; alert if request routing errors > 1% or queued requests > 200/s.

3) Key roles and responsibilities
- First responder (on-call engineer): Acknowledge, gather context, follow applicable runbook, and escalate.
- Incident Commander (IC): Owns triage and mitigation, coordinates communications and resources.
- Communications Lead: Publishes status page/customer updates and coordinates internal comms.
- Subject Matter Experts (SMEs): Service owners (runtime, infra, billing, security) who advise remediation and execute changes.
- Postmortem owner: Drafts and coordinates RCA within 72 hours of incident resolution.

4) Incident lifecycle (step-by-step)
1. Detection & Acknowledgement
   - Alerts fire into PagerDuty (or Slack for non-critical). On-call must acknowledge per severity SLA.
   - Triage: consult metrics (Grafana), logs (ELK), traces (Tempo/Jaeger), and recent deploys.
2. Triage & Classification
   - Confirm severity, affected services, estimated blast radius, and whether customer-visible.
   - If P0/P1, immediately appoint IC (typically senior on-call or SRE lead).
3. Mitigation & Containment
   - Follow the service-specific runbook (see Runbook Templates). Prioritize restoring customer experience over root-cause fixes.
   - Use safe remediation practices: prefer rollbacks, circuit breakers, traffic shaping, and throttles when applicable.
4. Communication
   - Internal first: Notify #incidents Slack, escalation channel, and relevant EM/PMs.
   - External: Communications Lead drafts status page update and customer-facing note. See 'Comms Templates' section.
5. Resolution & Recovery
   - Verify system health on metrics for at least two consecutive 5-minute windows and monitor for regression.
   - Leave detailed timeline and notes in the incident channel.
6. Post-incident (RCA & Action Items)
   - Postmortem owner creates a draft within 72 hours. Complete RCA, preventive actions, and assign owners for each action item.
   - Review in the Incident Review board and schedule follow-up changes.

5) Runbook template (service-specific)
- Title: <service-name> critical-path runbook
- Owner: <oncall-team-or-SME>
- PagerDuty trigger(s): (alert names and thresholds)
- Symptoms: (what will you observe)
- Initial checks (ordered):
  1. Check Grafana dashboard: error-rate, latency, throughput.
  2. Check recent deploys: CI/CD pipeline status and rolling deploys in the last 60 minutes.
  3. Check logs for error signatures (examples).
  4. Verify dependent services (e.g., kv-cache, model-router) are healthy.
- Quick fixes (ordered, with commands):
  - Rollback last deploy: kubectl -n prod rollout undo deploy/<service> --to-revision=<rev>
  - Recycle worker: kubectl -n prod scale deployment/<worker> --replicas=0 && sleep 10 && kubectl scale deployment/<worker> --replicas=<n>
  - Throttle non-critical routes via rate-limiter config: POST /admin/ratelimit
- Safety checks & approvals: list required approvals for infra changes, database migrations, or security work.
- Post-incident actions: add memory/CPU limits, circuit-breaker config, alert tuning, or a roll-forward plan.

6) On-call rotation, handoffs and expectations
- Rotation model: two-week primary on-call with one follow-on secondary on-call to assist (primary rotates weekly in pilot teams).
- Coverage hours: 24/7 for critical services; Monday–Friday 8:00–20:00 for lower-criticality services with weekend on-call as needed.
- Handoff checklist (must be completed in Slack or PagerDuty notes):
  1. Current incidents and status.
  2. Known flaky alerts and workarounds.
  3. Recent deploys and ongoing rollouts.
  4. On-call docs/runbooks you reviewed.
  5. Contact list for SMEs and out-of-band escalation.
- Escalation policy: primary -> secondary (5 minutes) -> on-call manager (15 minutes) -> SRE director (30 minutes). Adjust per severity.

7) Game days and proactive practice
- Purpose: validate runbooks, test cross-team coordination, and exercise paging/communications.
- Frequency: quarterly for core platform services, semi-annually for less-critical services.
- Game day checklist:
  - Pre-game: identify target scenario, freeze non-essential deploys, notify stakeholders, create a dedicated Slack channel.
  - During: run scenario (e.g., control-plane outage, KV cache saturation), observe response time, and record runbook fidelity.
  - Post-game: produce a short after-action summary and 90-day follow-up on high-priority action items.

8) Postmortem template and requirements
- Timeline: draft within 72 hours; final postmortem published within 14 days.
- Required sections:
  1. Title and incident date/time (UTC).
  2. Summary (one paragraph for execs).
  3. Impact (customers affected, downtime, SLA implications).
  4. Timeline (detailed, minute-granular).
  5. Root cause analysis (what failed and why).
  6. Contributing factors and detection gaps.
  7. Corrective actions (owner + due date) and long-term mitigations.
  8. Lessons learned and follow-up items.
- Approval: Postmortems for P0/P1 incidents must be reviewed by SRE and the product lead before publication.

9) Status page and customer communications templates
- Principles: be timely, transparent, consistent, and non-speculative. Prioritize customer impact and actionability.

Customer-facing examples (short, templated)
A) Initial acknowledged update (within 30–60 minutes of a P0/P1)
Subject: Incident — Service degradation affecting inference API
Body: We are investigating increased error rates and latency impacting text generation requests. Our engineers have acknowledged the issue and are actively triaging. We will post updates every 30 minutes or as milestones are reached. Affected customers may see errors or slow responses. We apologize for the disruption.

B) Status update (progress update)
Subject: Incident update — mitigation in progress
Body: Engineers have identified a routing regression in model-router caused by a recent config change. We have applied a temporary traffic-shaping rule and are seeing a 60% reduction in errors. We are validating and will provide a further update in 30 minutes.

C) Resolution notice
Subject: Incident resolved — inference API
Body: The routing regression has been reverted. All services are operating within normal parameters and p95 latency is back to baseline. Root cause analysis and next steps will be published in a postmortem within 14 days. We apologize for the impact.

Internal status page template fields (for operations team)
- Incident ID: IR-YYYYMMDD-###
- Affected services: list
- Severity: P0/P1/P2
- Start time: UTC
- Current status: investigating/mitigating/resolved
- Mitigation steps in progress: bullet list
- Customer-facing updates published: Yes/No (link)
- Next update ETA: timestamp

10) Storage, retention and linking
- All incident artifacts (Slack channel transcript, PagerDuty incident, Grafana links, postmortem) must be linked from the incident document and retained per policy.
- Postmortems are stored in confluence under /oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems with labels for easy search.

11) Metrics for continuous improvement
- Track MTTA (mean time to acknowledge), MTTR (mean time to resolve), and time-to-postmortem.
- Track action item completion rate (target: >90% closed or scheduled within 30 days).
- Use quarterly incident retros to update runbooks and alert thresholds.

12) Related resources and templates
- Runbook template: link to central runbook index (confluence page).
- PagerDuty on-call playbook: contact on-call-admin@redwood.com for admin changes.
- Status page management console: internal URL and credentials handling guidance (see security-and-compliance).

Appendix: Quick checklist for first 10 minutes of a P0
1. Acknowledge PagerDuty alert and set Slack channel.
2. Identify IC and Communications Lead.
3. Post initial customer-facing status on status.redwood.example (or customer email).
4. Verify safety of cross-region failover if needed.
5. If deploys in last 30 minutes, consider immediate rollback.

Document change log:
- 2024-07-12: Created by Maya Thompson.
- 2025-11-03: Updated severity definitions and SLO thresholds (reviewers: Diego, Priya).
- 2026-03-04: Added game day guidance and revised rotation policy for pilot teams.

Notes and links:
- Service owners must keep their runbooks up to date; automated reminders are sent monthly.
- For security incidents follow the security-and-compliance incident response process in addition to this playbook.

If you have updates or corrections to this playbook, submit a PR to the confluence draft and tag the oncall-sre team.
